q.t: Find the verb: The children played in the park.
q.e: ‘played’ is the action the children did.

q.t: Find the helping verb: She is singing a song.
q.e: ‘is’ helps the main verb ‘singing’ show the present continuous.

q.t: Past tense (V2) of go:
q.e: go is irregular: go – went – gone.

q.t: Past participle (V3) of write:
q.e: write – wrote – written.

q.t: Past tense of walk:
q.e: Regular verb: add -ed.

q.t: Choose the correct form: I have ___ my lunch.
q.e: After ‘have’ use V3: eat – ate – eaten.

q.t: Which verb is intransitive here?
q.e: ‘slept what?’ has no answer — no object, so intransitive.

q.t: Which sentence has a transitive verb?
q.e: ‘reads what?’ → a book. The action passes to an object.

q.t: -ing form of run:
q.e: Short vowel + single consonant → double it: running.

q.t: Past tense of cry:
q.e: Consonant + y → change y to i and add -ed.

q.t: Is has a main verb or helping verb in He has a red bicycle.?
q.e: No other verb follows it — ‘has’ itself means ‘owns’, so it is the main verb.

q.t: Is has a main verb or helping verb in He has finished.?
q.e: ‘finished’ carries the meaning; ‘has’ helps form the present perfect.

q.t: Choose the correct form: The bell has ___.
q.e: ring – rang – rung. After ‘has’ use V3.

q.t: Choose the correct form: They ___ to Goa last year.
q.e: ‘last year’ is a finished past time → simple past V2: went.

q.t: Choose the correct form: She has ___ the news.
q.e: hear – heard – heard.

q.t: Identify the linking verb: The milk smells sour.
q.e: ‘smells’ links ‘milk’ to the quality ‘sour’.

q.t: Choose the correct word: The flower looks ___.
q.e: ‘looks’ is a linking verb here — the word after it describes the flower, so it must be an adjective.

q.t: Past participle of begin:
q.e: begin – began – begun.

q.t: Find the error: I have went to Delhi twice.
q.e: After ‘have’ use V3: gone. ‘went’ (V2) never takes a helper.

q.t: Past tense of stop:
q.e: Short vowel + single consonant → double the p: stopped.

q.t: Is runs transitive or intransitive in My uncle runs a bakery.?
q.e: runs what? → a bakery. It has an object here, so it is transitive.

q.t: Choose the correct form: The hen has ___ an egg.
q.e: lay (put down) – laid – laid. A hen ‘lays’ (puts down) an egg.

q.t: Choose the correct form: He ___ on the bed all afternoon yesterday.
q.e: lie (rest) – lay – lain. ‘lay’ here is the past of ‘lie’.

q.t: Choose the correct form: The boy ___ to his mother about the broken vase. (did not tell the truth)
q.e: lie (tell an untruth) is regular: lie – lied – lied.

q.t: Which sentence can be changed into the passive?
q.e: Only a transitive verb (with an object: the cat) can become passive: The cat was chased by the dog.

q.t: Choose the correct form: The thief was ___ by the police.
q.e: catch – caught – caught. After ‘was’ (passive) use V3.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She felt sad after the match.
She felt sadly after the match.
She felt sadness after the match is.
She feeled sad after the match.
q.e: ‘felt’ is a linking verb here, so an adjective (sad) follows. feel – felt – felt.

q.t: Choose the correct form: Have you ever ___ a ghost?
q.e: see – saw – seen. After ‘have’ use V3.

q.t: -ing form of lie:
q.e: -ie changes to y before -ing: lie → lying, die → dying, tie → tying.

q.t: Which word is a verb? Please water the plants.
q.e: Here ‘water’ is the action (give water to). The same word can be a noun or a verb depending on its job.

q.t: Choose the correct form: The sun had ___ before we reached home.
q.e: set – set – set (all three forms the same, like put and cut).

q.t: Choose the correct form: He has ___ his book on the table.
q.e: He put the book down → ‘lay’ (put) – laid – laid.

q.t: Choose the correct form: The book has ___ on the table for a week.
q.e: The book is resting → ‘lie’ (rest) – lay – lain.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
q.e: ‘tastes’ links milk to a quality → adjective ‘sour’. ‘milk’ is singular → ‘tastes’.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
q.e: Here ‘tasted’ is an action (transitive), so ‘carefully’ (adverb) tells how she did it.

q.t: Find the error: The river has overflown its banks.
q.e: overflow is regular: overflow – overflowed – overflowed. ‘overflown’ belongs to ‘overfly’ (fly over).

q.t: Choose the correct form: The guests had ___ before the rain started.
q.e: arrive is regular — V3 is ‘arrived’.

q.t: In The leaves turned yellow., the verb turned is:
q.e: ‘turned’ means ‘became’ here and links leaves to the quality ‘yellow’. Nothing is being turned.

q.t: Choose the correct form: The shirt has ___ after washing.
q.e: shrink – shrank – shrunk. After ‘has’ use V3.

q.t: How many verbs (main + helping) are in: She must have been sleeping.?
q.e: must (modal) + have + been (helpers) + sleeping (main) = 4 words in the verb phrase.
